subject: general
question: What is the projected population of India by 2036, according to the National Commission on Population?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**1.52 billion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **National Commission on Population (NCP)**, the projected population of **India** by the year **2036** is expected to be **1.52 billion**__.
 
• The data is based on the **report "Population Projections for India and States 2011–2036"** prepared by the **National Commission on Population** under the guidance of the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, Government of India.
 
• This projection takes into account various factors such as **fertility rate, mortality rate, and migration trends** in India.
 
• With a population of **1.52 billion**, India is expected to remain the **second most populous country in the world**, following China, but it is anticipated that India may surpass China shortly thereafter.
 
• The population growth rate is expected to decline due to factors such as improvements in **healthcare, education, and family planning initiatives**.
 
• This population projection is critical for planning and implementing strategies in areas like **healthcare infrastructure, employment, education, and resource management**.
 
• The report also emphasizes the need for continued efforts in ensuring **sustainable development** to manage the challenges posed by a large population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Commission on Population (NCP)**__

 __
 
• The **National Commission on Population** was established in **2000** under the chairmanship of the **Prime Minister of India**.
 
• The aim of the commission is to monitor and review the implementation of the **National Population Policy (NPP), 2000**.
 
• The commission focuses on achieving **population stabilization** and improving the quality of life of citizens through better **health and family welfare programs**.
 
 
 
• **Fertility Rate**__
 __
 
• The **fertility rate** refers to the **average number of children born to a woman** over her lifetime.
 
• In India, the **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)** has been declining due to increased awareness and access to **family planning measures**.
 
 
 
• **Population Projections**__
 
 
• **Population projections** are statistical estimates of future population size and composition based on current data and trends.
 
• They are used by governments and organizations for **policy formulation and resource allocation**.
